OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind each publish, with every frontier release, a system or
model card whose dangerous-capability section reports how far the model is from automating AI
research. This site collects those AI R&D scores from the cards alone, with a source and a
confidence flag on every number. Use the menu on the left to flip between the labs; each lab page
opens with its graphs. How the data were collected and how to read the figures is on the
[Method and data](method.qmd) page.

## Reading across the three

Each lab measures a different thing under the AI R&D heading. DeepMind reports a single
human-normalized number on a public METR suite, then an internal research-engineering benchmark;
OpenAI reports pass rates on internal replication tasks and Kaggle-style competitions; Anthropic
reports fractions of a human baseline on internal tasks plus its own RE-Bench subset. SWE-bench
Verified is the only benchmark all three report, and even there the subset and scaffold differ.
The common thread is qualitative: every lab has moved from "well below human" statements in 2024
to reporting models at or above the human baseline on several-hour ML engineering tasks by 2026,
while each still judges the model below its own threshold for autonomous AI R&D. Two things to
watch when reading across cards: benchmark versions and subsets change (Terminal-Bench 1 to 2.0,
2.1 and 4.0; MLE-bench full to 30 to revised; RE-Bench 7 tasks to 5), and later cards re-run
earlier models and print different numbers, so a single model's score can differ between its own
card and a successor's comparison table.
